en.headline: Education chief says textbook prices up 3.6 per cent, rejects universal grant
en.dek: Christine Choi said the bureau is monitoring costs and has told publishers to avoid excessive packaging, while targeted subsidies remain available for low-income families.
body: Secretary for Education Christine Choi said on Saturday that textbook prices for the coming school year have risen by an average of 3.6 per cent, and that the Education Bureau is closely monitoring the situation.

Speaking on an RTHK programme after reports that a full set of secondary-one books could cost up to HK$7,000, Choi said that after excluding maps, dictionaries and exercise books the cost of required textbooks still stood at about HK$4,000 to HK$5,000.

Choi said the bureau has repeatedly urged publishers not to pursue overly elaborate printing and to keep production costs low. She added that the government already provides a textbook subsidy for low-income families and does not rule out offering more supporting materials in future.

On calls to lower the eligibility threshold for the subsidy or to restore a universal HK$2,500 student grant abolished in the 2025-26 school year, Choi said resources are limited and targeted support for families in genuine need is the preferred approach.

zh.headline: 蔡若蓮：教科書價升3.6% 關注價格問題 拒恢復通派津貼
zh.dek: 教育局局長表示局方密切監察書價，已要求出版商避免過度精美印刷，基層家庭繼續獲書簿津貼。
body: 教育局局長蔡若蓮周六表示，新學年教科書價格平均上升3.6%，局方非常關注並密切監察情況。
她在港台節目回應有報道指中一書單總額可達近7,000元時說，扣除地圖、字典及練習簿等參考書後，必需購買的教科書費用仍約4,000至5,000元。
蔡若蓮指局方一直與出版商保持溝通，要求勿追求過度精美印刷，盡量以低廉成本製作，確保質素之餘維持價格平穩。政府現時為有經濟困難家庭提供書簿津貼，亦不排除日後提供更多輔助教材。
對於放寬津貼入息審查或恢復不設審查的2,500元學生津貼，她表示社會資源並非無限，針對性支援真正有需要的家庭較為合適。
